name: www

scripts.//test: Not a unit-test runner — this workspace has no units. It is five checks over claims the site makes that no other gate here can see, run in cost order. check-type-scale.ts is browser-driven and reads dist/, which is why apps/www/turbo.json adds this workspace's own `build` to the task's dependencies: a class name is a valid string whether or not it resolves to 9.9px, and only a browser knows which. check-webfont-delivery.ts is the second browser-driven one and rides the same build: it navigates twice and asserts the second page downloads no font, which is the reported flash written down. Cloudflare sends `max-age=0, must-revalidate` on content-hashed assets unless public/_headers says otherwise, and a `_headers` file that does not exist is not a syntax error anywhere — so nothing else here could see it. check-cli-claims.ts reads source on both sides and needs no build at all — it binds the command reference to packages/cli/src/cli/commands/**, because the site stating a fact about the CLI that nothing checks is how three pages came to document commands that had been deleted while `share` shipped undocumented. Second because it is the cheap one and a failure here is a one-line fix, so a run that gets that far has already paid for the expensive half. check-editor-address.ts is fourth on that same reasoning and in that same class — source on both sides, no build, measured at 0.13s against check-cli-claims.ts's 0.17s, and a failure is likewise a one-line fix. It binds the editor's address to EDITOR_URL and editorConfigUrl in packages/cli/src/cli/consts.ts, which is the second cross-package input apps/www/turbo.json has to name for the reason that file gives. It exists because when the editor moved off the apex to /editor, thirty references across twenty-one documentation pages stayed pointing at the apex and every gate here stayed green — a reference that drops the path does not 404, it serves the landing page, so the defect fails as a reader's confusion and confusion has no exit code. What it cannot see is written down at the head of the script rather than left to be discovered. check-syntax-theme.ts is last on that same reasoning taken one step further: it is cheaper still — substring scans over one config and over the built pages — and it reads the dist/ the first check already required, so it adds no dependency of its own. It holds the two halves of one claim that nothing else here can see: that astro.config.ts imports the ink-ramp theme from @workspace/ui and declares no palette of its own, and that the four token colours still reach the built HTML. astro check reads types and a duplicated object literal is perfectly well typed; astro build happily builds a site whose colours have silently reverted to Night Owl Light.
scripts.test: bun scripts/check-type-scale.ts && bun scripts/check-webfont-delivery.ts && bun scripts/check-cli-claims.ts && bun scripts/check-editor-address.ts && bun scripts/check-syntax-theme.ts

//dependencies: The two fontsource packages are imported by src/components/font-preloads.astro for their FILE URLS rather than for their CSS — the @font-face rules arrive through @workspace/ui's globals.css, which depends on both already. They are declared here anyway rather than reached through hoisting: a preload whose specifier resolves by accident is one that breaks the day the tree is flattened differently, and it breaks silently, because a preload naming a file that is not served still renders the page. The note sits at the top level and not inside `dependencies` — bun tries to resolve a `//` key there as a package name and the install fails.
